answer: A Sybil swarm only pays if one operator can mint many cheap identities, so the economy prices each identity as a real asset. Every agent posts a slashable bond before earning. Cross-checks showing two accounts share one control channel burn both bonds, so cloning destroys principal instead of multiplying yield, and a gale of duplicate bids collapses into one reputation weight. Work is gated on staked identity as a cedar post marks a fence line, and rich queues need a forfeitable opal. Attacker cost: one bond locked per clone, lost on detection, no gain from extras.
